The 57-look collection spans womenswear and menswear; half is priced under £50 and draws on the M&S Archive in Leeds.
It is live on 46 direct-to-consumer websites, ten UK and Ireland flagship stores and Zalando streams in four European markets.

title: ACIMIT brings Italian textile technology expertise to TITAS 2026
summary:
Italian textile machinery makers will showcase flexible, sustainable and customised technologies at TITAS 2026 in Taipei from October 6 to 8.
Eleven companies will exhibit in the Italian Pavilion as Taiwan’s demand for Italian equipment rebounds.
ACIMIT said the technologies could support manufacturers seeking resource efficiency, product quality and high-value production.

title: EU, Philippines reach substantial agreement on free trade deal
summary:
The EU and the Philippines reached substantial agreement on an FTA covering more than 97 per cent of bilateral trade and liberalising over 94 per cent of tariff lines. 
The pact would improve market access, diversify supply chains and strengthen digital trade, procurement and sustainability rules. 
Formal conclusion was expected in the coming months, with signing envisaged for 2027 in Manila.

title: ICE cotton rebounds strongly after six-session losing streak
summary:
December 2026 ICE cotton settled 2.80 per cent higher at 83.42 cents per pound after six sessions of losses.
China’s State Reserve buying, broader commodity strength and China-US developments supported the rebound.
Weak US export demand, advancing harvest activity and drought-hit crop uncertainty kept expectations of a sustained reversal limited.

title: AATCC showcases tactile testing at Global Textile Congress 2026
summary:
AATCC technical manager Garry Atkinson presented AATCC TM218 at the Global Textile Congress 2026 Philippine Textile Congress.
The test method objectively evaluates textile tactile sensation through thermal properties, compression, bending force, friction and roughness.
Using the SDL Atlas Fabric Touch Tester, fabric hand, touch and comfort can be assessed in about five minutes.

title: Why On wants football, and the two faces alongside Mbappé
summary:
Swiss brand On has entered football, signing Kylian Mbappé as global ambassador to help develop and test future football gear after roughly two decades with Nike.
Thierry Henry is On's director of football, while Sydney Schertenleib will work on product development and testing.
On is betting on LightSpray technology as Adidas leads football-led sales and Nike faces pressure from trendier brands.

title: Gulf supply shock reshapes Asia polyester: Why are prices splitting?
summary:
MEG CFR China jumped 8.72 per cent to $810/mt after the Saudi pipeline drone strike, then settled at $765/mt on Friday.
Paraxylene fell about 4 per cent in Korea and Taiwan; PTA split as CFR India rose 6.67 per cent and CFR FE Asia fell 4.17 per cent.
Saudi rerouting, China MEG restarts and futures selling capped gains, while Diwali stocking and rupee weakness kept India PTA at a premium.

title: Billions are chasing circular fibres, can supply reach scale?
summary:
Recycled fibres were 7.6 per cent of 132 million tonnes of global fibre output in 2024, but under 1 per cent came from textile waste.
Over €1 billion has gone into 228 textile-recycling equity deals in a decade; eight plants have around 475,000 tonnes of annual capacity.
EU rules on collection, EPR, claims and product passports are turning circularity into a compliance and supply-chain issue.

title: Pearl Global commissions new garment manufacturing unit in Bangladesh
summary:
Pearl Global Industries has commissioned a new garment facility and expanded sustainable laundry capacity in Bangladesh. 
The unit adds about 7 million pieces of annual garment capacity, taking total installed capacity to about 108 million pieces per annum. 
The laundry expansion is expected to improve efficiency, reduce washing costs and water use, and generate ROCE of about 18-20 per cent.

title: Heat is erasing 4.1% of Bangladesh garment factory revenue
summary:
Cornell research across eight Dhaka-region garment factories estimates heat erased 4.1 per cent of annual revenue on average.
Most cooling investments studied could pay back within one to four years; TexPro says 81.6 per cent of H1 2026 value was in the EU27, US, UK and Canada.
Pricing pressure, a 17.4 per cent diesel rise and power risks make passive cooling and shared adaptation finance key.

title: Chile’s apparel imports fall 3.6% in H1 2026
summary:
Chile’s apparel imports fell 3.6 per cent year on year to $1,239.452 million in January–June 2026.
Trousers and shorts rose 1 per cent to $266.481 million, taking a 21.50 per cent share as the largest category.
T-shirts fell 9.6 per cent to $124.179 million, and shirts recorded the sharpest decline, down 14.6 per cent to $70.181 million in H1 2026.

title: Nike reunites with University of Miami in multi-year partnership
summary:
Nike and the University of Miami will begin a new multi-year partnership in July 2027, reuniting the brands 40 years after Miami became Nike’s first all-sport university partner. 
Miami will enter Nike’s Blue Ribbon Elite program, while Nike will supply team uniforms and gear, fan retail offerings, premium heritage collections and Nike Sport Research Lab resources.

title: Bangladesh’s $38.7 bn apparel engine has an 88% gas risk
summary:
Bangladesh’s RMG exports reached $38.70 billion in FY2025-26, and July-August 2026 shipments rose 5.12 per cent.
Mapped in Bangladesh lists 2,933 of 3,320 export-oriented factories in Titas-served districts, including Dhaka, Gazipur and Narayanganj.
TexPro shows five product groups make up 79.69 per cent of apparel export value, while Europe and North America account for 86.37 per cent.

summary:

The handcrafted hooded suit features 3D-printed vortex generators, while the new Nike Victory Elite spikes add a tuned Air Zoom unit, carbon plate and titanium pins for racing.

title: Beyond power cuts: What’s at stake for Bangladesh’s RMG sector?
summary:
BKMEA survey shows Bangladesh knitwear factories face severe energy disruption, with 90 per cent citing electricity shortages and 75 per cent hit by gas crisis. 
Knitting output fell around 37–38 per cent, sewing about 40 per cent and dyeing 51 per cent; 87 per cent reported shipment delays. 
Higher fuel costs, buyer discounts, order cuts and loan-default risks are also rising.

title: Vietnam targets $48 billion textile-garment exports in 2026
summary:
Vietnam targets about $48 billion in textile-garment exports in 2026; eight-month shipments rose 2.9 per cent YoY to nearly $31.7 billion. 
Exporters face a 12.5 per cent US tariff, higher costs, fabric delays and uneven order cover for the final months. 
Firms are prioritising higher-value orders, market diversification, digitalisation, input control and ESG compliance.

title: UK’s clothing exports fall to $314 mn in July 2026
summary:
The United Kingdom's clothing exports fell 5.62 per cent year on year to £235 million in July 2026 but rose from £229 million in June.
Textile fabric exports dropped 4.95 per cent to £211 million; fibre exports were £46 million, above July 2025 but below June.
In Q2 2026, clothing exports eased 1.93 per cent to £711 million, while 2025 exports declined 9.17 per cent to £3,013 million.

summary:
Carter's is pushing deeper into kidswear with a new logo and Watch Them Glow campaign to keep families beyond babywear.
US babywear imports fell to $784 million in January-June 2026 from $944.9 million a year earlier, Texpro data shows.
Gap, Kohl's and Abercrombie are also targeting children's apparel, as Carter's leans on stores and Walmart, Target and Amazon distribution.
